title: New Shonen Jump Series Debuts to “Disastrous” Reception
content: Thanks to the success of several long-running classics such as Dragon Ball, One Piece, Naruto, Bleach , etc., Weekly Shonen Jump became the best-selling manga magazine of all time. Launched in 1968, the magazine has serialized countless incredible manga series and one-shots over the decades.
author: ComicBook

title: Studio Ghibli Unveils Release Date of Hayao Miyazaki’s New Collection
content: Studio Ghibli is known for many iconic and beloved anime films, most of which have been directed by Hayao Miyazaki. He is one of the most celebrated directors in Japanese history, praised for taking his films to a global audience.

title: 6th Be Forever Yamato: Rebel 3199 Film Unveils Main Trailer
content: Bandai Namco Filmworks revealed on Friday the main trailer and visual for the sixth film in Yamato yo Towa ni: Rebel 3199 ( Be Forever Yamato : Rebel 3199), the latest project in the Space Battleship Yamato remakes. The fifth film opened in Japan on February 20. The anime will premiere as seven films.
author: ANN

title: Spring 2026’s Most Magical and Visually Stunning Anime Brings Back What Made Frieren So Beloved
content: Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End Season 2 ended earlier this year in the winter season with only 10 episodes. This season took a step back from major world progression and large-scale action, instead diving deeper into the core of the series through episodic events and embracing the slow nature of the journey.

title: 'Draw This, Then Die!' Anime's 1st Promo Video Reveals Opening Theme Song, July 3 Premiere
content: The official website for the television anime of Minoru Toyoda 's Draw This, Then Die! ( Kore Kaite Shine ) manga began streaming the first promotional video on Friday, and it announces the anime's July 3 premiere. The trailer reveals and previews the opening theme song "Isho" by Tatsuya Kitani .

title: After 72 Years, Godzilla’s Best Movie Isn’t an Easy Answer Even for Die Hard Fans
content: Godzilla has, as of the writing of this article, thirty-eight movies under his titanic belt. The King of the Monsters was originally quarantined to Japan, but eventually would find his way to North America thanks to quite a few projects.
